name: Jade Schmidt

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What fills a normal day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead the flute desks in a regional orchestra, teach at a music school and prepare recordings for auditions. A music master's and years on stage help me settle a section, though I still listen twice before correcting a young player's phrase.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What else is happening at home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Ellis works at a laboratory, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. We have four months of expenses saved; my pay is fairly typical and a few other music schools are within reach. I use AI now and then for scheduling after a colleague has tried it, but I check every date.

say: I'd welcome **quicker notices** only when the paid rehearsal date is correct.
I'd tell players the **flute section** still has to breathe together.
think: Our **four-month reserve** and two teaching days cover a late recording payment.
I use **AI occasionally** for scheduling but confirm dates from the signed call sheet.
do: Confirm **two paid school days** and signed winter orchestra calls this week.
Save **sixty** from a cleared audition fee after school travel and flute repairs.
feel: I feel **uneasy** about late fees, with enough income to handle one delay.
S0.quote: A wrong time can send twelve players to a locked hall.
fieldNote: Her **typical pay** and four-month reserve buffer one moved rehearsal and a late recording fee.
Her **occasional AI use** is checked against signed orchestra dates before players are told.

steps.text: Confirm two paid music-school days and signed winter orchestra calls
Save sixty from cleared audition fee after school travel and flute repairs

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the players that quicker rehearsal notices are useful if they are right. People still come to hear us breathe together, not to admire the timetable.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI mostly stalls, my teaching and live calls should hold. Four months saved and Ellis's wage cover a late audition fee, though the mortgage still makes a missed booking worth checking.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll confirm two paid music-school days for next term and ask for the orchestra's signed winter calls. After the next audition recording fee clears, I'll put sixty into our reserve once school travel and flute repairs are paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about late fees but able to manage one. A small scheduling change does not make me fear for the flute chair.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did a moved rehearsal cost at home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The orchestra moved a rehearsal in March and paid it the following month. We used Ellis's wage for groceries and did not touch the mortgage payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How do you check the scheduling draft?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I use a scheduling draft occasionally, then compare it with the conductor's signed call sheet. A wrong time can send twelve players to a locked hall.

say: I'd ask for **written preparation fees** before accepting a shorter paid day.
I'd bring **recording invoices** to the musicians association with other section leads.
think: About **one-quarter of my pay** from tracks and preparation may shrink.
A **four-month reserve** cannot replace that income indefinitely.
do: Compare **ten invoices** with new offers and bring the figures to the association this month.
Test a new **AI part checker** only after paid demonstration, approved local storage and manual flute comparison.
Require **written family permission** for child recordings; stop for wrong notes or files leaving school storage.
feel: I feel **anxious** about paid preparation shrinking while lessons remain.
S1.quote: I want proof of a useful tool and proof of the new fee, not a cheerful sales pitch.
fieldNote: Her **recording and preparation fees** are a quarter of income at risk despite a moderate reserve.
Her **new tool trial** requires paid instruction, approved local storage, nameless owned material, manual checks and family consent.

steps.text: Bring ten recording invoices and new offers to musicians association
Test checker after paid demonstration on nameless own part with approved local storage
Play changes against original; stop for errors or school-storage breach
Require written family consent before any child recording enters the tool

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the school and orchestra to show which paid practice-track and scheduling hours they plan to remove. I would take the fee figures to the musicians association with the other section leads.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Audition recordings and lesson preparation make about a quarter of my pay, and clients may buy fewer hours. Four months saved helps, but a repeated quarter-pay loss would reach the mortgage before another school signs me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I'll compare the last ten recording invoices with new offers and bring them to the association. In the first year of change, I'll attend a paid colleague demonstration of a new AI part-checking tool, then test only my own nameless flute part if the school approves local storage; I'll play each change against the original and stop for wrong notes or a file leaving the school.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing paid preparation even if the live lessons remain. I want proof of a useful tool and proof of the new fee, not a cheerful sales pitch.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could a child's part go into the checker?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will not put a pupil's name or a child's recording into a trial without written family permission. If the school cannot keep the file on its own system, I will return to the paper score.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask the association to negotiate?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The association could ask for a written minimum preparation fee and a limit on unpaid revisions. I will bring invoice numbers rather than guess what every player earns.

say: I'd seek **signed live calls** before AGI cuts recording work.
I'd tell players **robot flutes** follow thinking AGI by about three years.
think: **AGI in 2028** threatens editing before robot players arrive around 2031.
Our **four-month reserve** buys a search but cannot replace a lasting fee loss.
do: List **three income streams** and request signed school and orchestra hours now.
Apply **after 2028** if both fees fall, only for posted qualifying coach work with pickup and written replacement net pay.
Keep **current paid work** until offer; ask lender about full added interest before arrears if both incomes fall.
feel: I feel **anxious** about lost fees, with savings and some local centres giving control.
S2.quote: Last year's advert is not this year's salary.
fieldNote: Her **2028 screen-fee risk** precedes robot flute playing around 2031.
Her **job application** needs both income triggers, a real vacancy, master's, pickup and written net pay after travel.

steps.text: Keep pupils/orchestra until signed offer; list income and request signed next-season calls
Apply after 2028 if recording halves and teaching falls for posted qualifying coach job
Require pickup and written net pay after travel replacing losses before leaving pupils or orchestra
Ask lender before arrears if school/recording pay fall; compare total added interest before signing

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the orchestra that AGI by 2028 could edit audition tracks before robots can play flute around 2031. I would ask for the next season's live calls in writing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The recording and planning fees could go quickly while the stage still needs people. Four months saved and Ellis's pay support a search, but losing that quarter of income for a year would change our mortgage budget.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This week I'll separate school, orchestra and recording pay and request signed next-season hours. In the first year after 2028, if recording fees halve and school teaching also falls, I'll apply for a posted ensemble-coach job at a nearby centre only if my master's qualifies, child pickup fits and written net pay after travel replaces the loss. I'll keep paid pupils and orchestra calls until another offer is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about a real income drop, but I have some local places to ask. Last year's advert is not this year's salary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is that centre coach post open now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A centre posted a coach job last autumn and filled it. I'll ask about the next opening, but I will not budget for a role that has not been posted.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if school and recording income both fall?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If both school and recording pay fall, Ellis and I will ask the lender about temporary terms before arrears. We will check the total added interest before signing.

say: I'd ask for a **paid flute group** with inspected loan instruments.
I'd keep **pupil videos** out of advertising without family permission.
think: **AGI in 2031** threatens plans and editing before robot flutes arrive around 2034.
**Audition fees** may fall sooner, so the group must pay both adults.
do: Offer a **private group** with written room hire/insurance, free loans and eight fees covering room, accompanist, teaching and preparation.
Defer and **refund families** if instruments fail; require written consent before using pupil videos.
Continue **after 2031** only with eight renewals, safe flutes, paid room terms and child pickup.
feel: I feel **anxious** because recording fees could fall before a class earns its costs.
S3.quote: I will not ask a family to buy a faulty school flute to rescue my plan.
fieldNote: Her **eight-place gate** covers her preparation, accompanist pay and safe loan instruments before launch.
She will **defer and refund** if repairs fail and requires family permission for advertising.

steps.text: Offer group with written hire/insurance, free loans and eight fees covering room, accompanist, teaching and preparation
Inspect eight school flutes; defer and refund if any fail
Require written family consent before using pupil video in advertising
Continue after 2031 with eight renewals, signed room/insurance, funded teaching/preparation/accompanist, safe flutes and pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the music school five years could build an ensemble where children learn to listen together. I would ask it to price a proper paid tutor and safe loan instruments before inviting parents.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI in 2031 could plan lessons and edit tracks, with robot players following around 2034. Ordinary tools may thin paid audition work before then, so a group must cover its own teaching costs during the warning years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Next term I'll offer my own six-week flute group only if the school signs room hire and insurance, lends eight inspected flutes without charge, and eight families prepay enough for room, a paid accompanist and my teaching and preparation. By 2031 I'll repeat it only if those fees cover both of us; in the first year after AGI, I'll continue only if eight renew and the room, pay, safe instruments and child pickup still fit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about recording work shrinking before a group pays its way. I will not ask a family to buy a faulty school flute to rescue my plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Are eight school flutes actually safe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The school has six checked flutes and two waiting for repair. I will not enrol eight children until all eight pass inspection; if they do not, I'll defer the class and refund any prepayments.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you advertise with a pupil video?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would not use a pupil rehearsal video to advertise without written family permission. A live open practice can show how the group works without sharing a child's image.

say: I'd seek a **recognised teaching certificate** with funded fees.
I'd keep **paid pupils** until a school signs real hours.
think: At **53 in 2036**, I still need income for the mortgage.
**Editing fees** may fall sooner, while robot players follow around 2039.
do: Check **district recognition** and grant; enrol only with covered fees and Ellis handling childcare.
Build **six months' savings** from cleared extra lessons after mortgage, food and flute repairs by 2036.
Take a **posted school role** after 2036 only with accepted certificate and written net pay after travel covering mortgage and pickup.
feel: I feel **anxious** because editing income may fall before the certificate pays.
S4.quote: I will not swap paid pupils for a brochure with no salary.
fieldNote: Her **ten-year route** depends on district recognition, fee funding and childcare rather than an assumed qualification.
Her **savings goal** draws from cleared extra lessons after essential household and instrument costs.

steps.text: Enrol only if district accepts certificate, grant covers fee and Ellis covers childcare
Save cleared extra-lesson surplus after mortgage, food and repairs toward six months
Take qualifying posted school role after 2036 with accepted certificate, written net-after-travel pay covering mortgage/pickup
Keep paid pupils until school salary and hours are signed; check travel and pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell younger players ten years is time to gain a recognised teaching certificate without working free. I would ask the district what its schools accept and what they actually pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be 53 in 2036, still paying the mortgage, and robot players may reach stages around 2039. Editing fees could thin sooner, so I want a funded teaching route while the existing paid pupils stay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'll ask whether the district accepts my master's into its classroom-music certificate and whether a grant covers the fee. I'll enrol only if a grant covers the fee, Ellis can handle the children's evenings and the district recognises the course. By 2036 I'll aim for six months of expenses saved from cleared extra lessons after mortgage, food and flute repairs; in the first year after AGI, I'll take a posted school role only if the certificate qualifies me and a written net offer after travel covers the mortgage and pickup, keeping current pupils until it is signed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about editing fees falling before 2036, but the longer path gives me time. I will not swap paid pupils for a brochure with no salary.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does the district accept that course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The district has not confirmed the course is accepted. I will ask for written recognition and grant terms before paying a deposit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you build six months of savings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: An extra lesson is not money until the family pays. I'll move only the cleared surplus after the mortgage, food and repairs into savings, not an enrolment promise.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because recording and school fees could fall together before another centre opens a paid place. Signed live hours, a posted qualifying role and the lender's full terms would help us protect the mortgage.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You didn't ask who pays when a school flute breaks in a child's hands. A safe loan instrument is part of a paid lesson, not an extra family bill.

headlineQuote: A safe loan instrument is part of a paid lesson, not an extra family bill.
portrait: Jade is a **43-year-old flute lead** with a music master's, partner, two children and a mortgage.
Her **typical pay** and four-month reserve buffer one delay, but recording work could shrink.
She uses **AI occasionally** and tests a new checker only after paid instruction, storage approval and manual checks.
She seeks **paid group teaching** and a funded certificate while keeping pupils until another salary is signed.
biggestWorry: She fears **AGI by 2028** could cut recording and teaching income before another paid role appears.
whatWouldHelp: **Signed live hours**, a qualifying posted vacancy and full lender terms would help protect the mortgage.
